sermon.title: 2014 Easter Sunday
sermon.speaker: Speaker not named in the recording (not identified as Pastor Kincer)
sermon.summary: In this Easter message the speaker reviews the beating and crucifixion of Jesus and the miracles at His death, then teaches “God Bless You”: the blessing of Acts 3:26 is God turning us from sin. He uses Lazarus, Zacchaeus and Mary Magdalene as examples and a chemical demonstration to show how sin hurts us and those around us, ending with a prayer.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor note: the speaker is not named in the recording and does not sound like Pastor Kincer, so this page does not name him; please confirm. Several caption slips are corrected where the intended word is clear (for example “zakus” to “Zacchaeus” and “ar arthea” to “Arimathea”), and two spots are marked [unclear] (about the graves that were opened, and “the holy …” in the temple pattern). He says “Second Peter, or 1 Peter 2:9” and “Romans 3:23… or 6:23” while correcting himself. His comments about the soldiers’ numbers and the cleaning-products demonstration are his own and not verified here.

chunks.section_question: What did the soldiers do to Jesus before the crucifixion? (Matthew 27)
chunks.short_answer: The speaker says a whole band of soldiers scourged Jesus with a whip with pieces of glass and bone on the ends, put a crown of thorns on His head, mocked Him as King of the Jews, beat His head with a staff and plucked His beard. He says this is the Easter story and that the soldiers “delivered him up to be crucified.”

Jesus Christ went through the most horrific, horrible beating in all the world. Isaiah tells us that it was more disfigurement and scarring that any man suffered. When that whip went off on his back, you know, they just didn’t stop. There wasn’t a number they stopped it. They just kept going, and he bore that pain and that punishment for us, of course, as you know. And the blood of Jesus started to flow as they began to whip him, as they put put the crown of thorns on him. But you guys got to understand here, they took his garments, they stripped him. He didn’t have any clothes on. It’s embarrassing. He bore this embarrassment for us. He was naked on the cross. They put him up and everybody saw him, all of the people that were following him, the disciples that were there, John, Mary the mother. He was naked. That’s embarrassing. And they crucified Jesus. chunks.text: Now that’s, of course, a miracle, because there’s the sun’s supposed to be out, but God was doing something. So there was darkness over the whole land. They could see each other, but there was darkness, and it wasn’t smoke, it wasn’t an eclipse. God brought darkness. And at 3:00 p.m. Jesus gave up his spirit. The Bible says that no man could kill him. He had to give up his spirit. He had to let go. That’s important to understand. You see, nobody could come up and kill Jesus. If somebody cut off his arm, he could just put it right back on, healed it, and went on his way, cuz he’s God. Nobody could kill him. And as soon as he gave up his spirit, the earth quaked. The holy of holies was the place where you could come and meet with God, and you could all you had to be a certain person. You had to be a priest to go into that holy of holies. And God, not a man, he ripped it from the bottom, the top to the bottom, he ripped it in two.

chunks.section_question: What did the soldiers say when they saw the earthquake? (Matthew 27:54)
chunks.short_answer: He says the centurion and the men with him, “quite possibly the men that were whipping him,” saw the earthquake and the rocks split and began to fear greatly, saying “This was the Son of God.” He says they were not writing scripture but were witnesses who were convinced, and that God wanted to reach even those who whipped Him.
chunks.text:
Because God wasn’t sitting there alone on the cross. There were people watching and seeing these things, and you guys need to know that the Bible isn’t full of baloney. These are witnesses. These are people writing these records down. And in Matthew 27:54 it says, now, in “the centurion, and they that were with him.” You see, these men were quite possibly the men that were whipping him, the men that were beating him. When they saw all these things, when they saw the earthquake, he says that they were watching Jesus. They weren’t going around on doing their own thing. They were watching Jesus, and it says they saw the earthquake, they saw these things that were done, they saw the rocks split, they saw the darkness covered the land, and they began to fear in their hearts, saying, “What have I done? I just I just whipped Jesus. I just I just beat him over the head.” What if they feared greatly, saying, “This was the Son of God.” And here you have it. These people were not people that were writing the scriptures. They were just there seeing all this happen, and they were convinced in their heart this is the Son of God. Amazing.

And God wanted wanted to reach them. God wanted to reach those guys who whipped him, who took him out, who beat him over the head, who put the crown of thorns on him. You see, they were trying to suppress a king of the Jews. They didn’t know he was God until now. And fear fell upon them, and we know that many soldiers turned to Jesus. So let’s bow our heads this morning, and we just want to pray and thank Jesus this morning for his blood. Lord Jesus, we come before you this morning and we thank you for the blood that you shed on the cross. Lord Jesus, your blood covers all sin. God, your blood has no boundaries. God, there’s nothing that you cannot do with your blood. It is so powerful, God. Lord Jesus, we thank you for the cross, and Lord Jesus, we ask that you touch us with your blood and touch us with your spirit this morning. Amen.

chunks.short_answer: He says the story is “a message,” that Jesus calling “come forth” is about coming out of sin, and that sin kills our spiritual man. He cites Romans 6:23, that the wages of sin is death, and says Jesus can raise up our spiritual man and “loose us” from the bondage of sin as He did Lazarus.
chunks.text: He also said, “Loose him and let him go.” And this story is not just a miracle. It’s not just a healing. It’s not just an event, uh, some miraculous work. It’s a message this morning. We’ve got to understand that when Jesus called to Lazarus and said, “Come forth,” he’s talking about sin, coming out of sin. In Romans 3:23, the Bible says, or 6:23, it says that the wages of of sin is death. And you see, sin will kill our spiritual man. When when when sin is in control of our life, it kills our spiritual man. And you see, Jesus wants to call, he’s crying out to you, he’s saying, “Come forth. I can bring you out of sin. I can raise you up. I can raise your spiritual man up from the dead. I can do that for you. I can change you. I can loose you from the bondage that is holding you together.” You see, Lazarus was bound. He was in the tomb. There is no way for him to get out. But there was one way: Jesus Christ. And that is a powerful, the powerful message of his resurrection, that though we were dead in trespasses and sins, though we are, you know, were bound by sin, Jesus Christ can come and he can loose us and set us free from that.

chunks.section_question: How do we accept Jesus’ forgiveness? (Romans 3:23, Romans 6:23, 1 John 1:9)
chunks.short_answer: He cites Romans 3:23 that all have sinned, Romans 6:23 that the wages of sin is death but the gift of God is eternal life, and 1 John 1:9 that He is faithful and just to forgive. He leads a prayer to accept Jesus into your heart, admit you are a sinner, commit to doing right and “leaving the man of sin.”
chunks.text: Like Romans 3:23 says, “All have sinned and fallen short of the glory of God.” If you understand what it says in Romans 6:23, that the wages of that sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord. The Bible says in 1 John 1:9 that if you confess with your mouth and admit that you’re a sinner, he is faithful and just to forgive you of your sin and cleanse you from all unrighteousness. And pray this prayer with me: Lord Jesus, I accept you into my heart. I admit I am a sinner. I commit myself to doing the things that are right and leaving the man of sin. Thank you, Jesus, for cleansing me and forgiving me. Amen.

faqs.question: Why does he say the blood of Jesus is important?
faqs.answer: He says “that blood is the key… it’s the blood that allows us to be forgiven from sin. It covers our sin, and we need that blood.” He prays that Jesus’ “blood has no boundaries.”

faqs.question: Why does he say no one could kill Jesus?
faqs.answer: He says “the Bible says that no man could kill him. He had to give up his spirit,” and that if someone cut off His arm He could heal it, “cuz he’s God.”

faqs.question: What did the torn temple veil mean?
faqs.answer: He says the veil separated the holy of holies, where only a priest could meet with God, and that God ripping it in two from top to bottom fulfilled the new covenant, so that we can come to Jesus ourselves.

faqs.question: Does he say believers are priests?
faqs.answer: He cites 1 Peter 2:9, that we are “a special people, a holy priesthood,” and says that when we accept Christ we become a priest and can meet with Him ourselves.

scriptures.text_nkjv: But you are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, His own special people, that you may proclaim the praises of Him who called you out of darkness into His marvelous light;

faqs.question: Who does he say were witnesses at the cross?
faqs.answer: He says the centurion and the men with him, quite possibly the soldiers who beat Jesus, saw the earthquake, the rocks split and the darkness, and said “This was the Son of God.” He says this shows “the Bible isn’t full of baloney.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: So when the centurion and those with him, who were guarding Jesus, saw the earthquake and the things that had happened, they feared greatly, saying, “Truly this was the Son of God!”

faqs.question: Does he say prosperity is the blessing of God?
faqs.answer: He asks whether it is prosperity or miracles or healings and says the blessing in Acts 3:26 is God sending Jesus to bless us by turning each of you from sin. He notes much of the world lives in poverty.

scriptures.text_nkjv: To you first, God, having raised up His Servant Jesus, sent Him to bless you, in turning away every one of you from your iniquities.”

faqs.question: Why does he say Jesus waited for Lazarus to die?
faqs.answer: He says Jesus “purposely waited till he died before he came,” even though He knew Lazarus was sick, and then said “I am the resurrection, I am the life” and raised him after four days in the tomb.

faqs.question: What does he say sin does to us?
faqs.answer: He says “sin will kill our spiritual man,” and that Jesus calls us to “come forth” and loose us from the bondage.

scriptures.text_nkjv: For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.

faqs.question: Did Zacchaeus have to give up everything?
faqs.answer: He says no: “Don’t read this wrong… It doesn’t mean you got to become poor.” He says Zacchaeus gave half, paid four times back, and could still “provide for his family” and “live honestly.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Then Zacchaeus stood and said to the Lord, “Look, Lord, I give half of my goods to the poor; and if I have taken anything from anyone by false accusation, I restore fourfold.” And Jesus said to him, “Today salvation has come to this house, because he also is a son of Abraham;

faqs.question: What does he say about demon possession?
faqs.answer: He says Mary Magdalene was set free from seven demons, and that few people in America are possessed, “we don’t need to be possessed by demons,” we are “full of ourselves.”

faqs.question: Why does he say Mary was the first person to see the risen Jesus?
faqs.answer: He says it was “because she believed, she cared about Jesus,” she was at the crucifixion, burial and resurrection, and was “seeking Jesus.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: And many women who followed Jesus from Galilee, ministering to Him, were there looking on from afar,

faqs.question: What was the purpose of the water and cleaner demonstration?
faqs.answer: He says we start out pure and clean when we accept Jesus, but sin mixed back in makes “a toxic fume” that hurts our family and the people closest to us.

faqs.question: Why does he say we need the resurrection as well as the cross?
faqs.answer: He says “we need that blood… but we need his resurrection too… we got to have Jesus the resurrected Savior, the one who can pull us out of our sin.”

faqs.question: What does he say “such were some of you” means?
faqs.answer: He says Paul was writing to the church, telling them some used to be alcoholics, liars or sexually immoral, but Jesus “brought you out of those things” by the power of the resurrection.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And such were some of you. But you were washed, but you were sanctified, but you were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus and by the Spirit of our God.
